exact_statement: For every odd n>=511 and every complete adaptive single-coordinate restriction tree of uniform Maj_n, its scalar child-defect bill Lambda=sum_v w_v*j_v*log2(1+kappa_min,v/(2*j_v)) satisfies Lambda/I >= (n+1)/(4n)*log2(1+sqrt(3n+1)/20) >= log2(n)/8-1. Deleting all exactly isospectral active splits leaves Lambda_noniso/I >= (n+1)/(8n)*log2(1+sqrt(3n+1)/20) >= log2(n)/16-1/2. For every odd n>=3, Lambda_noniso<=Lambda<=I*(n-1)/n*log2(1/a_n)<=I*log2(2(n-1))/2, where a_n=2^(-(n-1))*binom(n-1,(n-1)/2). The good first-half nodes s^2<=n-d carry weighted j mass at least I/4 and child kappa_min>=1/5; good nonisospectral nodes carry at least I/8. Thus both scalar bills/I diverge with order log n.
hypotheses: odd uniform majority; all physical coordinates are independent fair signs
complete adaptive coordinate tree stops on constants and queries fresh coordinates only
kappa_min is the smaller actual maximum-Fourier-coefficient child defect
noniso means deletion of isospectral summands while restrictions continue, not granting leaf certificates
refutes: absolute finite K paying the LOG_ALLOCATION scalar Lambda by K I on complete majority restriction trees, even after deleting all exact-isospectral-node summands
